summary: Oddworld entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Oddworld: Abe's Oddysee
entries.definitive_edition: Original PC release for Abe's Oddysee; New 'n' Tasty separately for remake coverage

emulation.notes: Use native PC original for primary; use remake separately if desired.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PC release for original route; New 'n' Tasty PC for remake route

primary.version: Original Abe's Oddysee PC release, with New 'n' Tasty documented separately
primary.why: The queue title is the original 1997 game. New 'n' Tasty is a full remake with modern visuals and gameplay changes, so it should be documented as a secondary/remake route rather than replacing the original.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current PC original release through Steam/GOG. Record storefront/build, resolution/display wrapper, controller, save state, Mudokon rescue count, ending, and whether PlayStation original or New 'n' Tasty was compared.

secondary.why: PC is the practical capture route but PlayStation is the original console identity.

secondary.exclusive_content: Full remake with new visuals, audio, and gameplay changes
secondary.what_to_play: Track separately if playing the remake.
secondary.why: It is not the same game route as the 1997 original.

all_releases.fidelity: Original cinematic platformer release family; PC preferred for capture.

all_releases.platform: Oddworld: New 'n' Tasty on modern platforms
all_releases.fidelity: Full remake/reimagining with modern 3D visuals and gameplay changes.
all_releases.reason: secondary: separate remake route, not a replacement for original completion.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The remake has higher visual fidelity but is a changed route; the original 1997 game should remain its own archive target.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record whether playing original or remake; do not merge rescue counts/control behavior across versions.
